review_comments: Also this one. Please move to the third commit.

so the logic is broken now, as you accept now that the first empty msg is received, and then some data blobs again, and then the second empty msg.

I think it would be much nicer if we would simply accept either 1 or 3 fds on a final zero length msg. That's perfectly compatible with the current logic, a natural extension, and allows no vagueness about the protocol.

But what we accept is one aspect, second is what we send. 

During package updates/downgrades we may run into situation when message is generated by one version (older/newer ?) and processed by another version because in the meantime systemd-coredump got replaced. To cope with this I send two messages (first with 1 fd and second with 2 fds) and when processing I allow for at most two zero-length messages but so far I didn't check whether there are no data message in between them (they shouldn't be).
Please move this change to the earlier commit.
this should still be merged into previous commit

hmm, thinking about this more. If the protocol is extended here, I think it would make a ton of sense to extend it one step further at the same time, so that we do not have to go through the same dance a third time. Specifically, I think a 3rd fd should be passed along: the pidfd referencing the crashed process. note however, that old kernels do not support pidfds, hence it needs to be somewhat lenient on this, and support either 2 or 3 fds.

This goes beyond fixing some style and minor issues. This requires more in-depth look and I don't have the time for it. Is this something that needs to be done befor RC1 or can it wait for Michal to be back?

yes, it touches the protocol, I think this should be in rc1. does not have to be in this PR though, but I think it's crucial, because we go for pidfds everywhere, and it would suck if we have to do another iteration of this messy protocol augmenting again
Ok then we can keep the issue open with rc-blocker but let's get this PR merged so that the majority of other issues are solved, including the renaming. I'll link this comment in the issue.
afaics you don't need the `child` parameter anymore now. hence you can set that to NULL and get rid of the local var for it.
the removal of the local `child` variable should really be squashed into this commit (ended up in the next)
a debug log message would be good here btw

I mentioned this before: but the protocol is really weird, because it allows sending data, then sending the first trailing datagram, and then more data, and then the 2nd trailing datagram.

that's really strange and should be refused. (and it's aso different from the status quo ante, where the conneciton would be closed the instant the fd msg was received).
i.e. refuse any data to be passed through once the first sentinel message has been seen

you already log about all errors inside of gather_pid_mount_tree_fd(), hence this is strictly speaking duplicate logging.

i think it makes sense to keep a log message in place here however, if it tells us *new* stuff the original log messages inside of gather_pid_mount_tree_fd() didn't tell us yet. Specifically, it's the "ignoring" part which the function didn't mention. So maybe keep the log message mostly, but drop the %m (and change from log_warning_errno() to log_warning()).

that way, we will log about the error code once, and then log about the action we are taking because of it. (which is "no action")
Don't focus on commits, I made them separate so they are easier to review, maybe that was a bad idea.  I will probably just squash them.
